correctness.rationale: For a,b>=2 and P={0<=v_j<=u_i<=1}, the a+b+ab primitive facet normals are columns of a signed graph-incidence matrix on boundary nodes 0,1 and a+b coordinate nodes. Active edges at any face form subgraphs whose connected components cannot join 0 to 1. Their incidence matrix has totally unimodular nonzero maximal minors and saturated image, so the toric local class-group cokernel is free with rank equal to active-edge count minus rank, the cycle rank. Either p upper coordinates are 0 (forcing all lower 0, active block K_{p+1,b}, rank p(b-1)), or q lower coordinates are 1 (K_{q+1,a}, rank q(a-1)); these cases are disjoint. Otherwise every mixed active equality sits at unique common min upper/max lower value t in (0,1), yielding K_{r,s}, rank (r-1)(s-1), with other active stars acyclic. The alternative forest case is rank 0. TU makes all locally simplicial cones regular, hence local Q-factoriality iff smoothness. At fixed vertices maximal rank ab-min(a,b), versus Friedl global ab. A new independent complete face enumeration using vertex-set intersections and disjoint-set active-edge cycle counting confirmed the rank formula at every face for six (a,b) pairs (2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2),(2,4), with respectively 51,151,151,463,459,459 faces; this finite experiment is supplementary to the symbolic proof. Manually checked a=b=2 fixed vertices: empty vertex rank 0, one upper rank1, two upper rank2; separately read the supplied exact facecheck.py logic.
